question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
sql:
WITH daily_txn AS (
    SELECT customer_id, txn_date, SUM(txn_amount) as daily_net
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
),
date_range AS (
    SELECT customer_id, 
           MIN(txn_date) as min_date,
           MAX(txn_date) as max_date
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
all_dates AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT txn_date as date_val FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_date_range AS (
    SELECT dr.customer_id, ad.date_val
    FROM date_range dr
    JOIN all_dates ad ON ad.date_val BETWEEN dr.min_date AND dr.max_date
),
daily_balances AS (
    SELECT cdr.customer_id, cdr.date_val, COALESCE(dt.daily_net, 0) as daily_change
    FROM customer_date_range cdr
    LEFT JOIN daily_txn dt ON dt.customer_id = cdr.customer_id AND dt.txn_date = cdr.date_val
),
running_balances AS (
    SELECT customer_id, date_val, daily_change,
           SUM(daily_change) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY date_val) as balance
    FROM daily_balances
),
clamped_balances AS (
    SELECT customer_id, date_val, GREATEST(balance, 0) as balance
    FROM running_balances
),
monthly_max AS (
    SELECT customer_id, 
           substr(date_val, 1, 7) as month,
           MAX(balance) as max_daily_balance
    FROM clamped_balances
    GROUP BY customer_id, substr(date_val, 1, 7)
)
SELECT month, SUM(max_daily_balance) as monthly_total
FROM monthly_max
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
